title: Mathematics on arXiv — notable papers from 7 October 2026
global_caveat: Inferred selection, not an official arXiv trending ranking. arXiv supplies no official trending chart; citation evidence is extremely limited this soon after announcement, and the listed results are new preprint claims, not independently verified proofs.

sections.title: Non-perturbative finite connectivities in supercritical Bernoulli percolation on Z^d with d>=3
sections.abstract: The authors derive sharp Ornstein–Zernike asymptotics for finite-cluster connectivity throughout the supercritical regime of nearest-neighbor Bernoulli percolation on Z^d, d>=3.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract and introduction claim sharp Ornstein–Zernike asymptotics for finite-cluster two-point connectivity for all p>p_c in the stated model and dimensions, using volume control and adapted coarse-graining/irreducible-cluster methods.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Nearest-neighbor bond percolation on Z^d, d>=3, p>p_c(d); the event is connection by a finite cluster.
sections.unique_caveat: Does not cover criticality, dimension two, or arbitrary long-range models; new preprint claim.

sections.title: Compactness and Noncompactness for the Positive Yamabe–Escobar Problem with Minimal Boundary
sections.abstract: The author establishes compactness ranges and constructs noncompact sequences for the positive-scalar-curvature, minimal-boundary Yamabe–Escobar problem, with sharp dimension thresholds across metric classes.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims compactness for 3<=n<=14 in the general setting and sharpness by examples for n>=15; corresponding thresholds are 18 for locally conformally flat metrics and 20 for umbilic boundary.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Positive constant scalar curvature and minimal boundary on the hemisphere setting; thresholds depend on the metric/boundary class.
sections.unique_caveat: Conclusions are dimension- and class-specific; detailed hypotheses for constructed families require the full proofs.

sections.title: Optimal bound for the polynomial Littlewood–Offord problem
sections.abstract: For a fixed-degree multilinear polynomial with r pairwise variable-disjoint top-degree monomials, the author claims an O_d(r^-1/2) zero-probability bound under independent Rademacher inputs.
sections.claimed_result: The author states P[F(xi)=0]=O_d(r^-1/2) for degree-d multilinear F with r disjoint degree-d monomials, plus a related small-ball estimate; the paper says this resolves stated Nguyen–Vu and total-influence conjectures.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed degree d, multilinear polynomial, independent Rademacher variables, and r pairwise disjoint supports of nonzero degree-d monomials.
sections.unique_caveat: The author says GPT-6 Pro discovered the proof, which the author then checked and rewrote; this report has not independently verified it. Applies to the stated structured setting.

sections.title: Relative isoperimetry in the three-dimensional cube: classification and quantitative stability
sections.abstract: The authors claim the complete relative isoperimetric profile and all minimizers in the unit cube, along with a sharp quadratic stability estimate and consequences for stated open problems.
sections.claimed_result: Up to symmetries and complementation, minimizers are corner eighth-balls, edge quarter-cylinders, and coordinate slabs, transitioning at 4π/81 and 1/π; perimeter deficit controls squared L1 distance with optimal exponent two.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Relative perimeter and fixed-volume sets in the three-dimensional unit cube.
sections.unique_caveat: The classification is domain-specific; the abstract's cuboid consequence covers (0,beta)×(0,1)^2 with 0<beta<=1.

sections.title: Random independent sets in uncrowded hypergraphs
sections.abstract: For fixed uniformity and large degeneracy, the authors obtain an asymptotically sharp fractional-chromatic-number bound for hypergraphs of girth at least five.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed k>=2 and sufficiently large d, the maximum fractional chromatic number is (1+o_d(1))*((k-1)d/log d)^(1/(k-1)) for k-uniform, d-degenerate hypergraphs of any fixed girth g>=5.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed uniformity k and girth threshold g>=5, with degeneracy d tending large.
sections.unique_caveat: The main formula is asymptotic in d and excludes hypergraphs with short cycles below the stated girth threshold.

sections.title: New algebraic points on covers of elliptic curves
sections.abstract: Under suitable hypotheses, the authors bound fields admitting new points on degree-n covers of elliptic curves and prove density-zero results in degrees two through five.
sections.claimed_result: For suitable hypotheses, the discriminant count up to X of primitive degree-n fields with a new point is O(X^1/2) or O(X/(log X)^alpha); density zero is obtained in degrees 2–5, with a primitive degree-four result and eight quadratic-field examples for bielliptic modular curves.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Genus-at-least-two curves over Q covering elliptic curves; quantitative results require hypotheses specified in the paper.
sections.unique_caveat: Density conclusions apply only under stated hypotheses and to specified degrees, not all covers or all number-field degrees.

sections.title: Coordinate isoperimetric mass and a positive mass theorem for distributional scalar curvature
sections.abstract: The authors use coordinate isoperimetric mass to establish its invariance and a positive mass theorem for low-regularity asymptotically flat metrics with nonnegative distributional scalar curvature.
sections.claimed_result: For W^{1,p}_{-tau} asymptotically flat metrics with p>n and tau>(n-2)/2, the coordinate isoperimetric mass is coordinate invariant and equals generalized ADM mass; positivity holds without added topological assumptions beyond asymptotic flatness.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Weighted Sobolev regularity, decay, asymptotic flatness, and nonnegative distributional scalar curvature as specified in the abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is stated for the given regularity and decay range; endpoint exponents are not covered by the abstract.

sections.title: The Kuranishi space of joint deformations of Calabi–Yau manifolds and holomorphic vector bundles
sections.abstract: The author studies joint deformations of complex manifolds and holomorphic vector bundles, proving unobstructedness under conditions and constructing both unobstructed and obstructed examples.
sections.claimed_result: For a Fujiki manifold with torsion canonical bundle and H^2(X,End^0 E)=0, the author claims unobstructed joint deformations; in the trivial-canonical case three weak ddbar conditions can replace the Fujiki assumption. Obstructed pairs are also constructed.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Joint deformations of compact complex manifolds X and holomorphic bundles E→X; unobstructedness depends on the stated geometric and cohomological hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: There is no blanket unobstructedness result; vanishing and geometric assumptions matter, and the paper gives obstructed examples.

sections.title: Global large-data solutions for the BGK equation with physical collision frequency in a slab
sections.abstract: The authors claim global renormalized solutions for a slab BGK problem with density-dependent collision frequency from finite-mass, finite-energy, finite-entropy data, without smallness or pointwise bounds.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim global renormalized solutions for the BGK equation in a slab with physical density-dependent collision frequency, for inflow and Maxwell boundary conditions under the stated data assumptions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Initial data have finite mass, kinetic energy, and entropy, with corresponding inflow-flux bounds; no smallness or positive lower bounds on density or temperature are imposed.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract claims existence of renormalized solutions, not uniqueness or classical regularity; the result is specific to the slab and stated boundary/data assumptions.
